messages:
kyle_infra: Starting a staged terraform apply for release v1.14.0 — change window 23:00-01:00 UTC. Plan includes: IAM role rename redwood-deploy -> redwood-runner, route table update to add TGW route to 10.40.0.0/16, and a backend lock upgrade for tfstate. Tagging @marta_sre @amy_platform for ack. Main concern: cross-account IAM trust change requires coordination and rollback plan.
marta_sre: Thanks. What's the rollback plan if the role rename breaks cross-account assume? We should avoid deleting the old role until consumers have switched.
kyle_infra: Agreed. Plan is to create the new role alongside the old one, attach policies, then flip consumers via staged config. Current plan shows `aws_iam_role.redwood_runner` will be replaced (create+delete).
deploy-bot: Deploybot: terraform plan succeeded (plan id: p-9f3). No resource deletions except role replacement. Lock acquired on tfstate backend s3://redwood-terraform-state/prod. Approve with `/deploy approve p-9f3`.
amy_platform: Please pin `provider.aws` to 5.8.0 in provider.tf for this run; newer provider changed AssumeRole behaviour and can break cross-account flows.
kyle_infra: Done, updated provider pin and re-ran terraform plan — plan id p-9f4. Pushing plan output to internal gist: https://internal.gist/abcd. Also will apply `-target=aws_iam_role.redwood_runner` in the first pass to minimize blast radius.
sam_engineering: Can we do a canary? Apply role change in staging + a canary prod account first, verify login path and auth metrics, then roll to full prod. Timeline ok?
marta_sre: Agree. Also request to notify oncall for 30m after apply for metric checks. @zach_oncall can you monitor auth errors and PD thresholds?
zach_oncall: Yep — 23:30-00:00 I'll watch auth logs and PagerDuty. Set a 15m post-apply check window.
deploy-bot: Deploybot: `terraform apply` started for plan p-9f4 on kyle_infra-runner. Command: ```terraform apply -auto-approve -lock-timeout=15m -target=aws_iam_role.redwood_runner```
deploy-bot: Deploybot: apply completed for target role. No errors. New role created: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-runner. Consumers validated via quick smoke auth tests. Other changes remain pending.
kyle_infra: Applying the rest of changes now; will do phased route update (canary AZ first) with `-parallelism=10`.
deploy-bot: Deploybot: apply failed while updating route table rtb-0abc: target VPC not found in account 210987654321. Error: `Error: InvalidVpcID.NotFound`. Rolling back the route change.
sam_engineering: That route target is referencing an old TGW attachment id. Can we revert only the route change? What's the status of the new role — are services still using the old role or the new one? If role is stable, revert route changes and hold routing changes.
kyle_infra: Rolled back the route update with `terraform apply -target=aws_route_table.assoc -refresh=false` to remove the faulty change. Role is stable and consumers passed smoke tests. I'll open a PR to pin tfstate lock timeout and add a canary gating step.
marta_sre: Good catch. Add a temporary routing hold and schedule the second apply in the morning window if needed. Please document rollback steps in #incidents and tag with `infra-apply` and timestamps.
kyle_infra: Rollback snippet pasted to the incident thread: ```# rollback route change
terraform apply -auto-approve -target=aws_route_table.assoc -var 'release=v1.14.0'
# if tfstate corruption suspected, restore from s3://redwood-terraform-state/backups/2026-03-20```
zach_oncall: No auth regressions observed during the 30m monitor. I recommend final apply tomorrow 02:00 UTC after infra review :thumbsup:.
amy_platform: Also add provider pin note to the release changelog: `provider.aws = "~>5.8.0"` and call out the IAM alias/assume-role caveat in release notes.
